name: Troy Burne
fine: Unofficial re-creation built from the mapped course layout (© OpenStreetMap contributors), USGS 3DEP elevation and published hole descriptions. Not affiliated with Troy Burne.
tips: A long, mostly flat opener that tightens as it goes. Three stacked bunkers left and three more right squeeze the lay-up zone, and sand rings a raised green — fourteen traps in all.
A lake runs the whole left side and two large bunkers pinch the landing area. Water sits left of the green and three bunkers guard the right, so choose your miss.
Two very deep bunkers guard the front left and front right. A spine runs across the green, so land it on the right side of the ridge.
The one par 4 you can think about driving. Twelve bunkers defend it, four around the green, but the putting surface is one of the tamest on the course.
Straight and gently downhill, and still a three-shotter for most. Five fairway bunkers catch loose drives and four more wrap the green.
A wall of clustered bunkers crosses the fairway straight ahead. The green is the wildest around — it falls hard from back to front with a sneaky false front.
An elevated tee with a view over the whole hole. Three stacked bunkers sit right of the fairway, a small pot guards the front of the green, and a collection area waits behind it.
A long, dangerous par 3. The big, deep bunker left of the green pulls in tee shots like a magnet.
A long par 4 with ten bunkers, but it finishes on the easiest, flattest green on the course — a real chance to close the front nine well.
A strong dogleg left. A long waste bunker runs down the left side, and a pond lurks left of the approach — cut the corner and you bring both into play.
The signature hole. A pond sits right of the line on the way in, and the bunkers left of the green are the most punishing on the course — deep and steep.
A reachable par 5 that hugs the shoreline on the left from tee to green. Eight bunkers and an elevated three-tier green make the second shot a real decision.
A lengthy par 3 with the lake down the left and a pond protecting the right side of a big green.
One of the hardest tee shots out here: lake on the left, a cluster of bunkers in the right side of the landing zone, and a little waterfall pond by the approach.
The shortest hole with the toughest green. A spine snakes across the putting surface and putts break faster than you expect.
The longest hole: the pond it shares with 10 sits left of the tee-shot landing area. The final approach climbs to a green perched well above the fairway.
A stunning downhill par 4 with a pond tucked right of the green, so favour the left on the approach. Bunkers line the left side of the fairway.
A long par 4 with no tricks. Two big bunkers sit right, fescue waits for a wide miss, and a deep hollow lurks short left of the green.
